summary.title: Tetris in ClojureScript
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build the core of a Tetris game in ClojureScript by step-by-step evolving an immutable board, piece coordinates, and an atom-based game state.
keywords: how to write tetris in clojurescript
takeaways: Represent the Tetris board as a vector of row vectors and pieces as lists of relative [x y] coordinates.
Rotate pieces with a simple coordinate transform and check legality with a piece-fits? collision test before applying moves.
Implement gravity, soft drop, and hard drop by moving the piece and locking it into the board when it can no longer move.
Detect and clear full rows, then collapse remaining rows, and add animation and timed gravity using core.async channels.
summary.summary: This is an animated, interactive slide presentation by shaunlebron that walks through building a Tetris game in ClojureScript, focusing on design patterns. It starts with an empty board as nested vectors, defines the seven piece shapes as coordinate lists, and adds movement and rotation helpers. It then covers collision checks, locking pieces, hard and soft drop, filled-row detection and clearing, and finally timed gravity, held-key input, and a game-over sequence using core.async. The page notes it assumes some prior ClojureScript knowledge.
